patch_description:
The recommendation targets the key weakness observed across generations: all search effort concentrates on a single basin (the best lattice layout explored by one SA trajectory), and longer runtimes did not translate into better radii (the 2.56s multi-start run scored no better than the 0.56s constructor, while the short 0.9s greedy climb reached 2.40 — the best so far). Combined score also rewards low eval_time, so the budget should be modest (~1.4s), not 2.2–2.7s.

Changes:
1. Enrich the seeding pass with scale variants (0.98, 1.0) so the "best basin" is chosen from a wider lattice family — more diverse basins to jitter around.
2. Replace the simulated annealing block with the recommended multi-start jittered greedy hill-climb: each of 4 starts perturbs the winning lattice with its own ±0.01 Gaussian jitter (distinct seed per start, decorrelating the basins per the Gen-8 lesson), uses the proven adaptive-step move set (1–3 circles per move, shrink-when-stuck / occasional-grow), and receives a shrinking per-start time share `(deadline − now)/(n_starts − start)` so early starts explore broadly while the last start does fine polish. Total budget is capped at 1.4s to keep eval_time near the regime that scored 0.91, while the multi-start jitter gives more independent chances to escape local optima that a single greedy or SA trajectory cannot.

This directly combines the two mechanisms that individually produced the best results (multi-start jitter diversity from program 2, short-budget adaptive greedy from program 4) while avoiding the time-bloat that hurt programs 2 and 3.
